title: A Thorn for the Salt
premise: Orsen Halloran, a nonbinary charm-seller hiding their gatekeeper bloodline in the magic-outlawed city of Saltmere, discovers that the old gods are answering prayers again because the seal on their ancestral gate is failing. Hunted by both the Inquisitors who outlawed magic and the god-touched zealots who want the gate opened, Orsen must choose between restoring the seal with their own life or letting the gods return and reigniting an ancient war. With help from Sefa, an Inquisitor's daughter torn between love and duty, Orsen learns the gate was never meant to be shut forever—only balanced. In the end, Orsen rebinds the gate not with sacrifice but with shared guardianship, opening a fragile new era where magic and mortals coexist under watch.
about_author: Rosalind Okafor is a former archivist of coastal folklore who writes fantasy rooted in tide, salt, and stubborn hope. She lives between two harbors and insists that every locked door deserves a better question.

chapters.title: Charms for the Godless
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. In Saltmere's night market, Orsen sells harmless charms while concealing the faint hum of the sealed gate beneath their shop. A child's prayer is answered by something old, and the ward-stones in Orsen's cellar crack. Emotional beat: quiet dread—the decade of invisibility is ending.

chapters.title: The Prayer That Answered Back
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Investigating the cracked wards, Orsen hears the gate whisper their true name—a name they buried ten years ago. They realize the seal is tied to their bloodline and failing. Emotional beat: identity resurfacing; fear of being known.

chapters.title: Salt and Cinders
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa, an Inquisitor's daughter cataloguing reports of answered prayers, covers for a god-touched beggar and begins doubting her father's crusade. She traces the anomalies to the night market. Emotional beat: duty cracking against conscience.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Sefa confronts Orsen at the shop; instead of arrest, an uneasy bargain forms—she'll bury her report if Orsen shows her the gate. Below the city, they witness the seal bleeding light. Emotional beat: wary alliance, first spark of trust.

chapters.title: The Zealot's Bell
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The god-touched cult, led by the radiant Veyra, finds Orsen and demands they open the gate as the last Halloran. Orsen refuses; Veyra marks them, making their presence visible to every believer in the city. Emotional beat: hunted, exposed, alone.

chapters.title: A House of Small Denials
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Her father uncovers her deception and gives her an ultimatum: deliver the gatekeeper or share the pyre. Sefa burns her own files and warns Orsen, severing herself from family and rank. Emotional beat: love chosen over inherited duty.

chapters.title: Ten Years Under the Floor
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Fleeing through the undercity, Orsen finally tells Sefa the truth: they didn't just inherit the gate—they helped seal it as a teenager, erasing their own magic to survive. Emotional beat: confession, grief, intimacy deepening into love.

chapters.title: The Gate Remembers Its Name
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Veyra breaches the seal from above while Inquisitors storm from below; the gate tears half-open and the first old god steps through, hungry for worship and war. Emotional beat: catastrophe—every choice has failed.

chapters.title: Balance Is a Door Held by Two
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. Orsen realizes the seal was never meant to be solitary: it requires two keepers, one of the bloodline and one of the law. Orsen and Sefa bind themselves to the gate together, holding it open-but-ordered as Veyra falls into the threshold. Emotional beat: sacrifice transformed into partnership.

chapters.title: A City That Prays Carefully
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV, closing with Orsen's. Months later, Saltmere negotiates with the patient lesser gods; charms are legal again, watched but welcome. Orsen and Sefa keep the gate side by side, no longer invisible, no longer alone. Emotional beat: belonging found—not in hiding, but in being held.
